full_judgment: 2. The case of the appellant was that on 1.9.1950 he took on lease the premises of a Cinema House, then known as the New Paradise Talkies, for a period of 15 years by a registered deed at a monthly rent of Tk. 600/00, for the purpose of exhibiting Cinematograph Films in the said premises. In respect of the films exhibited in the said premises he paid amusement tax under the Bengal Amusement Tax Act, 1922 by purchasing adhesive stamps which were affixed to Cinema Tickets issued to Customers.
